name: Recruiter Direct Note
template: Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your updates hiring for {{company}} engineering. I build with {{primary_skill}}, recently {{proof_point}}. Would value connecting here as relevant openings take shape.
description: Establish a direct connection with a technical recruiter hiring for target engineering teams.
toneNote: Concise and respectful of recruiter screen volume; leads with verified stack and one proof point.
altOpeners: Hi {{recipient_name}}, noticed your focus building {{company}}'s tech bench.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your team is actively sourcing for {{role}} roles at {{company}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, came across your profile while tracking engineering hiring at {{company}}.
whenToUse: When connecting with a tech recruiter who explicitly posts about engineering hiring.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for engineering managers or peer engineers.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday to Thursday between 9:30 AM and 11:30 AM.
followUpNote: If no acceptance within 10 days, leave the request open and follow up via email if an opening goes live (followup-gentle).

name: Recruiter InMail Value Proposition
subject: {{role}} candidate: {{your_name}} ({{primary_skill}})
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I specialize in {{primary_skill}} and recently {{proof_point}}. With {{company}} expanding the {{role}} team, I wanted to put my profile in front of you directly.

My focus has been writing clean, tested services and understanding production failure modes. You can review my code samples and past implementations here: {{portfolio}}.

If my background matches what your engineering managers are evaluating this quarter, could we schedule a brief 10-minute introductory call?

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Secure a quick recruiter screening chat by presenting verifiable project impact and stack alignment.
toneNote: Direct, polite, and scannable without corporate fluff.
altOpeners: Having built multiple production-grade services in {{primary_skill}}, I am reaching out regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
My hands-on engineering work focuses on {{primary_skill}}, and I have been following {{company}}'s engineering milestones.
I specialize in {{primary_skill}} and recently wrapped up work where I {{proof_point}}.
whenToUse: When you have InMail credits and the recruiter manages the specific requisition for your role.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when the company only accepts applications through campus placements or designated TPO coordinators.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is mid-week morning hours for highest response likelihood.
followUpNote: Follow up after 6 business days with value-add-follow-up if unread.

name: Cold Email Direct Role Application
subject: Application: {{role}} - {{your_name}} ({{primary_skill}})
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I saw the {{role}} opening posted for {{company}} and wanted to share my technical background directly.

I work primarily with {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. My project code and architecture notes are documented at {{portfolio}}.

Given the requirements for {{role}}, I would welcome the opportunity to complete an initial technical assessment or speak with your team.

Are you available for a brief conversation this week to discuss next steps?

Sincerely,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Submit a clean, evidence-based cold application directly to the designated talent scout.
toneNote: Clear, crisp, and respectful of high inbound volume.
altOpeners: I saw the {{role}} listing posted for {{company}} and am submitting my details directly.
Following {{company}}'s recent hiring update for {{role}} engineers, I am sharing my technical profile.
I noticed the active {{role}} requisition on {{company}}'s careers portal and wanted to share my fit.
whenToUse: When an active job posting exists and you have verified the recruiter's corporate email address.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the company explicitly requests applicants not to email recruiters directly.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday or Wednesday mornings.
followUpNote: Follow up with gentle-follow-up after 5 business days if no reply.

name: Cold Email Scannable Bullet Pitch
subject: {{your_name}} - {{role}} profile ({{primary_skill}})
description: Provide an ultra-scannable 3-line overview that can be digested in under 15 seconds.
toneNote: Minimalist, structured, zero conversational preamble.
altOpeners: Are you still evaluating candidates for the {{role}} requisition at {{company}}?
Is the {{role}} position at {{company}} still actively open for applications?
Could you confirm if your team is currently reviewing profiles for {{role}}?
whenToUse: Ideal for busy recruiters managing multiple high-volume roles simultaneously.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when a detailed narrative of systems architecture or research context is required.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday mornings around 10:00 AM.
followUpNote: Use final-polite-loop-closure if no response after 7 days.

name: Hiring Manager Project Hook
template: Hi {{recipient_name}}, followed the public write-up on {{company}}'s {{admired_project}}. As an engineer working in {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}. Would value connecting to keep up with your engineering team's work.
description: Connect with an engineering manager by referencing concrete admiration for an engineering system they oversee.
toneNote: Technical peer respect without flattering or begging.
altOpeners: Hi {{recipient_name}}, came across your team's work scaling {{admired_project}} at {{company}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, read through {{company}}'s recent engineering updates regarding {{admired_project}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, noticed your team's technical decisions around {{admired_project}} at {{company}}.
whenToUse: When connecting with team leads, engineering managers, or directors whose teams built a specific public feature.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you cannot name a genuine product or technical initiative.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early morning (8:30 AM to 9:30 AM) before standup meetings.
followUpNote: If connected, let 3-4 days pass before sharing an engineering question (prospective-teammate-stack-question).

name: Hiring Manager High-Impact Pitch
subject: {{role}} candidate: {{your_name}} (focused on {{primary_skill}})
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I noticed your group at {{company}} is hiring for the {{role}} opening. My core stack centers on {{primary_skill}}, and recently I {{proof_point}}.

Given the complexity of {{admired_project}}, I have focused on writing modular code with high unit test coverage and low latency overhead. You can inspect my implementations directly at {{portfolio}}.

Would you be open to a 10-minute introductory conversation to see if my skill set matches your team's roadmap?

Warmly,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Pitch immediate engineering contribution directly to the hiring manager with verified metrics.
toneNote: Pragmatic, execution-focused, and humble about learning curve.
altOpeners: Having spent the last few quarters shipping projects in {{primary_skill}}, I am writing regarding your {{role}} opening.
I focus on building resilient software in {{primary_skill}}, and saw that your group at {{company}} is adding engineers.
I track the technical milestones your team ships at {{company}}, particularly around {{admired_project}}.
whenToUse: When reaching out to the direct hiring manager for an open headcount.
whenNotToUse: Do not send to general recruiters or non-technical business partners.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday between 9:00 AM and 11:00 AM.
followUpNote: Follow up with value-add-follow-up after 6 business days.

name: Peer Engineer Tech Conversation
subject: Quick technical question regarding {{company}}'s {{primary_skill}} stack
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I was reviewing {{company}}'s engineering setup and saw your work as a software engineer on {{admired_project}}.

As someone developing in {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}. I ran into interesting trade-offs around concurrency and schema migration, and wondered how your team approaches this problem in production.

If you have two minutes between sprints, what is one design trade-off you found critical when building {{admired_project}}?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Start a grounded engineer-to-engineer dialogue about stack choices and team development habits.
toneNote: Curious, professional, and respectful of active coding time.
altOpeners: How does your team at {{company}} balance architectural refactoring against fast delivery on {{admired_project}}?
What led your engineering team at {{company}} to adopt your current approach on {{admired_project}}?
How does your day-to-day workflow at {{company}} handle service reliability on {{admired_project}}?
whenToUse: When connecting with software engineers on target teams to understand team culture before applying.
whenNotToUse: Never ask a peer engineer for an immediate referral in this initial contact.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is late afternoon around 4:30 PM after daily scrum commitments.
followUpNote: If they provide a thoughtful answer, thank them and keep warm with give-first-note.

name: Cold Email Solutions & Problem Solving
subject: Small prototype related to {{company}} {{admired_project}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I built a lightweight prototype addressing a common performance bottleneck in {{admired_project}}: {{portfolio}}.

I work primarily in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. Looking at {{company}}'s public engineering priorities, I wanted to see if this design pattern aligns with how your team plans upcoming quarters.

Could I ask for your brief technical feedback on this repository when you have a moment?

Sincerely,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Present a concrete solution prototype or architectural observation directly to an engineering lead.
toneNote: Solutions-oriented, builder mindset, zero ungrounded critique.
altOpeners: I put together a small implementation exploring how {{company}} could approach {{admired_project}}.
While studying {{company}}'s engineering milestones on {{admired_project}}, I built a functional prototype.
I have been experimenting with solutions that mirror the architectural scope of {{admired_project}}.
whenToUse: When you have written a public repo, demo, or reproducible code sample relevant to the team.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the prototype link is broken, private, or unfinished.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is mid-week morning.
followUpNote: If no reply after 7 days, follow up using gentle-follow-up.

name: Alumni Common Ground
template: Hi {{recipient_name}}, fellow alum from {{college}} here! Great to see your work at {{company}} on the engineering team. I am preparing for {{role}} roles with a focus on {{primary_skill}}. Would love to connect and follow your journey.
description: Establish connection with a college alumnus currently working at the target organization.
toneNote: Warm, respectful of shared college heritage, with zero immediate asks for jobs.
altOpeners: Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw another {{college}} graduate making an impact at {{company}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, coming across {{college}} alumni at companies like {{company}} is always inspiring.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, greetings from a fellow {{college}} graduate.
whenToUse: Strictly for alumni who graduated from the same university or college institution.
whenNotToUse: Never send to recruiters or hiring managers who did not attend your college.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early evening (6:00 PM to 8:00 PM) when alumni catch up on personal networks.
followUpNote: After connecting, wait 4-5 days before reaching out with alumni-warm-referral-ask.

name: Alumni Warm Referral Ask
subject: {{college}} student inquiring about {{role}} referral at {{company}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I hope you are having a productive week. As a fellow graduate from {{college}}, I have been tracking {{company}}'s engineering milestones.

I am preparing to apply for the {{role}} opening (Job ID: {{job_id}}). Over the past year, I have built production projects in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}.

If you feel comfortable, would you be open to submitting an internal referral on {{company}}'s employee portal? My resume and project links are available at {{portfolio}}.

Completely understand if timing or company policy prevents this, and thank you for your time either way.

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Request an internal employee referral from an alumnus after mutual context has been established.
toneNote: Humble, structured, forwardable fit summary, explicit no-pressure out.
altOpeners: As a fellow {{college}} alumnus, I have been following your career journey at {{company}} with great interest.
Reaching out as a {{college}} junior preparing for off-campus opportunities at {{company}}.
Following up on our alumni connection, I wanted to share my recent engineering preparations for {{company}}.
whenToUse: When applying for an open job ID where an alumnus works at the company.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for strangers with whom you share no alumni or mutual bond.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday early evening.
followUpNote: If no reply after 10-12 days, send a low-pressure referral status nudge (referral-status-nudge).

name: Mutual Connection / Peer Referral
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, noticed our shared connection through {{referrer_relationship}} in the {{primary_skill}} community. I have been following {{company}}'s work, particularly {{admired_project}}.

I am exploring the {{role}} opening, and recently {{proof_point}}. Could I ask for 10 minutes of your advice on how your team evaluates candidates during the technical interview?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Reach out to a peer or warm contact through a mutual acquaintance or community context.
toneNote: Casual but polite, establishing warm relationship bridge.
altOpeners: I noticed we share connections across the {{primary_skill}} developer community.
Saw that we are both connected with mutual peers working in {{primary_skill}}.
Came across your updates through our shared network in the tech ecosystem.
whenToUse: When you share a mutual contact, community group, or former teammate with the recipient.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you have never interacted and have zero shared connections.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday afternoons.
followUpNote: If no response after 7 days, let the thread rest.

name: Referral Recommendation via Team Lead
subject: Application pathway for {{role}} at {{company}} - {{your_name}}
description: Inquire directly with an engineering lead on the preferred application pathway.
toneNote: Courteous, direct, and considerate of protocol.
altOpeners: Would your engineering group at {{company}} prefer that I apply for {{role}} via internal referral or direct portal submission?
What is the most effective way for a candidate with {{primary_skill}} experience to get their profile before your team for {{role}}?
Should I submit my application for {{role}} directly through {{company}}'s careers site, or does your team review incoming referrals first?
whenToUse: When you know someone inside the company but want to confirm the hiring lead's preferred workflow.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the application instructions explicitly specify single-channel submission.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday morning.
followUpNote: Use gentle-follow-up after 6 business days if no reply.

name: Gentle Follow-Up (Day 5-7)
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Following up briefly on my note sent {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.

I understand your schedule is demanding, so keeping this concise: I remain eager to be considered and have continued building in {{primary_skill}}.

If you need any additional code samples ({{portfolio}}) or availability details, I am happy to share them. Is this position still open for consideration?

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
description: Send a polite, low-friction status check referencing original message context without sounding aggrieved.
toneNote: Calm, patient, concise, acknowledging crowded inboxes.
altOpeners: Following up briefly on my earlier note regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
Checking in on my previous email sent {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago about the {{role}} role.
Wanted to send a quick follow-up to my earlier message regarding {{company}} engineering.
whenToUse: Send 5 to 7 business days after initial cold email or application if no reply has been received.
whenNotToUse: Do not send within 72 hours of first outreach; allow reasonable processing time.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday or Wednesday morning around 10:00 AM.
followUpNote: If still no response after another 7 days, transition to final-polite-loop-closure.

name: Value-Add Follow-Up with Update
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Following up on my note last week regarding {{company}}'s {{role}} team. Since reaching out, I {{proof_point}} and documented the architecture here: {{portfolio}}.

This implementation directly relates to the scalability challenges we discussed around {{admired_project}}.

Would you have 10 minutes this week to discuss how this approach aligns with your current technical roadmap?

Warmly,
{{your_name}}
description: Follow up by introducing new, verifiable evidence or milestone shipped since the original touchpoint.
toneNote: Proactive, growth-oriented, evidence-driven.
altOpeners: Since reaching out last week regarding {{company}}'s {{role}} team, I shipped a fresh technical milestone.
Wanted to follow up on my earlier note with an update on my recent engineering work.
Checking back in regarding the {{role}} team with a newly published project update.
whenToUse: When you have accomplished a tangible milestone (e.g. deployed a new feature, fixed a bug, wrote a benchmark).
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you have no new concrete technical progress to share.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is mid-week morning.
followUpNote: If unacknowledged after 7 days, send final-polite-loop-closure.

name: Final Polite Loop Closure
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Circling back one last time regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.

If the hiring priority has shifted or timing is not right, I completely understand. I will continue tracking {{company}}'s engineering milestones and would welcome staying in touch on LinkedIn for future cycles.

Thank you for your time and consideration,
{{your_name}}
description: Gracefully close the communication loop while keeping doors open for future hiring cycles.
toneNote: Gracious, zero bitterness, completely releases the recipient from pressure.
altOpeners: Circling back one final time regarding the {{role}} position at {{company}}.
Sending a final note to close the loop regarding my application for {{role}} at {{company}}.
Reaching out one last time regarding {{company}}'s {{role}} opening.
whenToUse: Send as the final touchpoint after 2 prior messages have received no reply.
whenNotToUse: Never send before at least one prior follow-up has elapsed.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Friday afternoon or mid-week.
followUpNote: No further follow-up on this role. Re-engage only after 3-6 months with a major milestone (reapply-after-rejection).

name: Founder Cold Email - Product Observation
subject: Quick observation on {{company}}'s {{admired_project}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I have been testing {{company}} and noticed {{specific_observation}}. It made me think about how your team handles that edge case at current user volume.

I am an engineer focused on {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. My code and architectural explorations are at {{portfolio}}.

If you have 10 minutes this week, I would value hearing how your early engineering team prioritizes improvements in that area.

Best,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Initiate a dialogue with a startup founder grounded in a concrete, verified user observation of their product.
toneNote: Sharp, respectful, focused on the product experience rather than self-aggrandizement.
altOpeners: While using {{company}} recently, I noticed an interesting pattern in {{specific_observation}}.
I have been testing {{company}}'s latest release and observed how {{specific_observation}} performs.
As an active user of {{company}}, I observed something specific about {{specific_observation}}.
whenToUse: When you genuinely use or tested the startup's product and discovered an authentic UX or technical observation.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked if specific_observation is empty. Never fabricate a fake bug or generic comment.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early morning (7:30 AM to 8:30 AM) before daily operations kick in.
followUpNote: If unread after 6 days, follow up with build-first-prototype if you have built a fix.

name: CTO Stack Question DM
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw {{company}}'s technical updates on {{admired_project}}. As someone building in {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}.

Quick engineering question: what factored most into your choice between managed cloud primitives and self-hosted components for {{admired_project}}?

Curious about the trade-offs you encountered.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Ask a targeted, single technical question to a startup CTO regarding an architectural decision.
toneNote: Engineer-to-engineer, technically rigorous, zero pleasantry overhead.
altOpeners: What led your engineering team at {{company}} to select your current architecture for {{admired_project}}?
Quick technical question regarding {{company}}'s backend choices around {{admired_project}}.
Curious about the concurrency design your team implemented for {{admired_project}} at {{company}}.
whenToUse: When messaging a technical co-founder or CTO on Twitter, LinkedIn, or developer channels.
whenNotToUse: Never ask a non-technical CEO or HR partner about deep stack primitives.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday evenings or Sunday afternoon.
followUpNote: If they answer, thank them and keep warm with build-first-prototype.

name: Founding Engineer Scope Pitch
subject: Early engineer candidate for {{company}} - {{your_name}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I know early-stage teams at {{company}} need engineers who can take feature scope from whiteboard to production without hand-holding.

I am a fresher specializing in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. I understand I have fewer years of formal tenure, but I compensate with high shipping velocity, automated test discipline, and comfort reading unfamiliar codebases (code: {{portfolio}}).

Could we schedule a 15-minute call this week to see if my builder background fits your current roadmap?

Best,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Pitch your readiness to take high ownership and ship quickly as an early-stage software engineer.
toneNote: Hungry, humble about years of experience, transparent about speed and reliability.
altOpeners: I know early-stage teams need builders who can take a feature from spec to production without hand-holding.
As a fresher who prioritizes execution speed and clean testing, I want to contribute to {{company}}.
I specialize in {{primary_skill}} and focus on shipping end-to-end features rapidly.
whenToUse: When applying to seed, pre-Series A, or Series A startups looking for high-ownership builders.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for large multinational corporations or campus placement cell drives.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early morning or late evening.
followUpNote: Use gentle-follow-up after 5 business days.

name: Build-First Outreach - Small Prototype
subject: A small prototype for {{company}} {{admired_project}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I use {{company}} and noticed potential in {{admired_project}}. Rather than sending a cold resume, I put together a working prototype of how that could work: {{portfolio}}.

I am {{your_name}}, an engineer working with {{primary_skill}}. Recently, I {{proof_point}}.

If this looks interesting, could I ask for 5 minutes of your feedback on whether this technical approach is sound? No worries at all if your team is already exploring other directions.

Best,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Demonstrate initiative by building a working prototype or feature demo before asking for anything.
toneNote: Builder-first, respectful, no resume attached, focuses entirely on working software.
altOpeners: Rather than just sending a resume, I spent the weekend building a prototype related to {{admired_project}}.
I put together a functioning demo showing how {{company}} could approach {{admired_project}}.
To demonstrate my alignment with {{company}}'s product, I implemented a small proof-of-concept.
whenToUse: When you have built a tangible working demo, public GitHub repo, or live deployment specifically for this team.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked if portfolio/demo link is empty. Never attach a PDF resume to this touchpoint.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday morning.
followUpNote: Follow up with value-add-follow-up after 7 days if unread.

name: Response to a "We're Hiring" Post
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your recent post looking for a {{role}} at {{company}} via {{source_trigger}}. As an engineer focused on {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}.

My code samples and system designs are at {{portfolio}}. Would love to connect and submit my background for this requisition.

Best,
{{your_name}}
description: Respond immediately to an executive or recruiter hiring broadcast with zero fluff and immediate fit summary.
toneNote: Direct, rapid-response, references the specific hiring update.
altOpeners: Saw your hiring post regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
Reaching out directly in response to your recent update looking for {{role}} engineers.
Noticed your post seeking engineering talent for {{company}}'s {{role}} team.
whenToUse: Within 24 to 48 hours of a founder, CTO, or team lead posting a public hiring update on LinkedIn or Twitter.
whenNotToUse: Do not quote extensive paragraphs from their post beyond the role name and context trigger.
sendWindowNote: Send as quickly as possible while the post is still generating active recruiter engagement.
followUpNote: If accepted, follow up with recruiter-inmail-value-prop or email.

name: University Relations Eligibility Query
subject: Eligibility inquiry for {{company}} graduate hiring ({{batch_year}} batch)
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Could you confirm if {{company}}'s upcoming graduate engineering intake will be open to students from the {{batch_year}} passing batch?

I am currently completing my degree at {{college}}, specializing in {{primary_skill}}. Over the last year, I {{proof_point}} (projects and repository links: {{portfolio}}).

If off-campus registrations are scheduled, where can our college batch register for official screening updates?

Thank you for your guidance,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Inquire with university relations coordinators regarding graduation batch eligibility and intake windows.
toneNote: Formal, polite, educational-context aware, respectful of recruitment timelines.
altOpeners: Could you confirm if {{company}}'s graduate engineering drive is open to the {{batch_year}} passing batch?
I am inquiring regarding the eligibility criteria and timelines for {{company}}'s {{batch_year}} campus intake.
Does {{company}}'s university relations program currently accept applications from {{batch_year}} graduates?
whenToUse: When targeting university relations, talent acquisition leads, or campus recruiters before placement season starts.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for experienced hiring managers or lateral engineering requisitions.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is August through October, or January through March in Indian academic calendar.
followUpNote: Follow up after 10 business days if unread, or check official university portal announcements.

name: Off-Campus Fresher Drive Follow-Up
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Following up on my registration and assessment submission for {{company}}'s off-campus drive (Application ID: {{job_id}}).

I completed the online technical evaluation on {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago and wanted to confirm if results for the {{batch_year}} batch have been finalized.

My primary stack is {{primary_skill}}, and my project work remains accessible at {{portfolio}}. Could you share an update on the schedule for technical interview rounds?

Thank you,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Follow up on an off-campus recruitment drive assessment or registration with explicit application tracking ID.
toneNote: Patient, process-respecting, includes application identification details.
altOpeners: Following up on my submission for the {{company}} off-campus drive (Application ID: {{job_id}}).
Checking in regarding next steps for the {{batch_year}} graduate intake under Job ID {{job_id}}.
Submitting a status check regarding the {{company}} off-campus assessment for {{job_id}}.
whenToUse: After completing an online assessment (OA) or national qualifying test for an off-campus fresher intake.
whenNotToUse: Do not send within 7 days of test completion, as bulk grading takes time.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is mid-week morning.
followUpNote: If no reply after 14 days, assume the batch cohort is processing and check spam folder.

name: Intern-to-PPO Conversion Note
subject: Internship wrap-up & full-time discussion - {{your_name}}
description: Initiate a structured conversation with your internship manager or HR partner regarding pre-placement offer (PPO) conversion.
toneNote: Professional, appreciative, grounded in internship deliverables and metrics.
altOpeners: As my internship period at {{company}} approaches its conclusion, I wanted to schedule a discussion about full-time conversion.
Reflecting on the projects shipped during my internship at {{company}}, I would value a conversation about returning full-time.
With my internship deliverables completed on the {{role}} team, I am reaching out regarding post-graduation opportunities.
whenToUse: Strictly for active or recently completed interns evaluating full-time return offers (PPOs).
whenNotToUse: Incompatible if experience_level is not Intern.
sendWindowNote: Send 3 to 4 weeks before the scheduled internship end date.
followUpNote: Follow up in your regular 1-on-1 meeting or check with HR coordinator.

name: Campus Drive Process Question to Alumnus
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, greetings from {{college}}! {{company}} is visiting our campus for the {{batch_year}} placement drive, and I am preparing for the software engineering screen.

My background is centered on {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. Could I ask for 10 minutes of your time to understand what fundamental concepts your team evaluates most during coding rounds?

Not asking for any referral since it is an on-campus drive, just looking for genuine preparation advice.

Thank you,
{{your_name}}
description: Ask an alumnus from your college for guidance on preparation topics and interview structure for an upcoming campus drive.
toneNote: Humble, respectful of senior colleague, zero referral pressure.
altOpeners: As a {{college}} junior preparing for {{company}}'s upcoming on-campus recruitment, I would value your perspective.
{{company}} is visiting {{college}} for placements this semester, and I am preparing for the technical rounds.
Reaching out to a fellow {{college}} graduate ahead of {{company}}'s recruitment drive on our campus.
whenToUse: When the company is visiting your campus through the official Training & Placement Cell (TPO).
whenNotToUse: Do not ask for a referral, as campus drives operate through placement cell policy.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early evening during the weeks leading up to campus visit.
followUpNote: If they share insights, send a thank-you note and update them post-interview.

name: Ask Placement Cell to Forward Profile
subject: Profile submission for {{company}} campus drive - {{your_name}} ({{batch_year}} batch)
description: Provide your college placement office (TPO coordinator) with a structured, verified profile summary for company shortlists.
toneNote: Formal, institutional, structured according to Indian TPO conventions.
altOpeners: Submitting my technical summary for inclusion in the {{company}} placement shortlist.
In accordance with the placement cell circular for {{company}}, I am providing my verified profile details.
Sharing my candidate overview for the upcoming {{company}} on-campus engineering drive.
whenToUse: When submitting details to your university placement officer (TPO) or student placement coordinators.
whenNotToUse: Do not send to external corporate executives or founders.
sendWindowNote: Send during active placement cell registration windows before deadlines.
followUpNote: Check the internal college placement notices or WhatsApp/Telegram announcement channel.

name: OSS Contribution to Maintainer
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I recently submitted a pull request on {{company}}'s open-source repo for {{admired_project}} (PR: {{pr_link}}). I work with {{primary_skill}} and wanted to ensure my patch aligns with your project style guidelines.

Could you share if your maintainer team prefers handling unit test fixtures inline or via shared mock modules?

Happy to adapt the implementation based on your review.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Connect with an engineer or core maintainer at the target company around an authentic open-source pull request.
toneNote: Collaborative, open-source native, humble, zero transactional overtone.
altOpeners: I recently opened a pull request on {{company}}'s open-source repository ({{pr_link}}).
Following {{company}}'s open-source projects, I submitted a PR addressing {{admired_project}} ({{pr_link}}).
I have been contributing to {{company}}'s public tooling and recently submitted {{pr_link}}.
whenToUse: When you have submitted a genuine pull request or issue to an open-source project maintained by the company.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked if pr_link is empty. Never claim a contribution you did not author.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday afternoon or during public triage hours.
followUpNote: Respond on GitHub PR reviews directly before sending any additional direct messages.

name: Engineering Blog Reaction
subject: Thoughtful takeaway on your {{company}} post regarding {{admired_project}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I read your recent engineering post on how {{company}} scaled {{admired_project}}. Your breakdown of database replication lag and idempotency guarantees was especially clarifying.

As someone developing with {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}. It made me wonder how your service handles network partitions during peak failover.

If your schedule permits, would you be open to a 10-minute technical exchange about your production findings?

Warmly,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Engage with an engineering blog author by discussing technical takeaways and trade-offs rather than generic flattery.
toneNote: Intellectually curious, specific, cites genuine architectural details.
altOpeners: I read your recent article detailing how {{company}} architected {{admired_project}}.
Your engineering blog breakdown on {{admired_project}} at {{company}} provided concrete architectural clarity.
Following your team's publication on {{admired_project}}, I was fascinated by the trade-offs you outlined.
whenToUse: When an engineer or tech lead at the target company published a technical blog post or whitepaper.
whenNotToUse: Never use empty praise without mentioning a specific architectural takeaway.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is mid-week morning.
followUpNote: If they respond, thank them for their time and maintain warm contact.

name: Product Teardown - Small Improvement Note
subject: Lightweight analysis and benchmark for {{company}} {{admired_project}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I put together a lightweight performance teardown examining client asset caching on {{company}}'s {{admired_project}}: {{portfolio}}.

I specialize in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. My goal was exploring how localized tree-shaking and preconnect headers could shave 200ms from the initial render.

Could I ask for your brief take on whether these observations align with your current performance backlog?

Sincerely,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Share a constructive, non-security UX or performance teardown highlighting potential optimisations.
toneNote: Humble, respectful of existing constraints, strictly non-adversarial.
altOpeners: I ran a brief bundle size and client-side latency audit on {{company}}'s {{admired_project}}.
While studying {{company}}'s frontend load times, I documented three small optimization opportunities.
I put together a brief technical teardown analyzing asset caching on {{admired_project}}.
whenToUse: For sharing non-sensitive UX, accessibility, or web-performance benchmark analyses.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked for security vulnerabilities. Security bugs must be reported via security.txt or bug bounties.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday or Wednesday morning.
followUpNote: Follow up with gentle-follow-up after 7 business days if unacknowledged.

name: Hackathon / Project Demo Share
subject: Built a hackathon prototype for {{admired_project}} domain - {{your_name}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

At a recent hackathon, my team engineered a working prototype designed around problem spaces that {{company}} tackles in {{admired_project}}. A live demo and repository are hosted at {{portfolio}}.

As the lead developer writing in {{primary_skill}}, I {{proof_point}}. Given your team's active work in this domain, I wanted to put my work directly in front of you.

Could we schedule 10 minutes this week to discuss how this domain experience maps to your open {{role}} headcount?

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Share an award-winning or domain-matched hackathon project with an engineering manager in the same domain.
toneNote: Energetic, builder-driven, focused on solved domain problems.
altOpeners: At a recent engineering hackathon, our team built an application solving challenges in the {{admired_project}} space.
I recently built an end-to-end prototype tackling problem spaces very similar to {{company}}'s {{admired_project}}.
Following {{company}}'s developments in {{admired_project}}, I designed a hackathon project exploring this problem.
whenToUse: When you have built a hackathon submission or comprehensive side project in the company's exact domain.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the portfolio link does not host a working deployment or readable codebase.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday morning.
followUpNote: Follow up with value-add-follow-up after 6 business days.

name: Post-Meetup / Webinar Follow-Up to Speaker
template: Hi {{recipient_name}}, your point on {{talk_topic}} at {{event_name}} changed how I think about system design. I am an engineer developing in {{primary_skill}}. Would love to stay connected and follow your team's engineering posts at {{company}}.
description: Follow up with a conference speaker or webinar host by referencing their specific talk insights.
toneNote: Appreciative, professional, grounded in the speaker's thesis.
altOpeners: Hi {{recipient_name}}, really appreciated your keynote covering {{talk_topic}} at {{event_name}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, attended your presentation at {{event_name}} discussing {{talk_topic}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, your session on {{talk_topic}} at {{event_name}} was one of my favorites.
whenToUse: Within 48 hours of attending a tech conference, local meetup, or webinar where the recipient gave a talk.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you did not actually attend the talk or cannot cite the topic.
sendWindowNote: Send within 24 to 48 hours while the conference session is fresh in memory.
followUpNote: If connected, engage with their technical posts before asking any career questions.

name: Hackathon Sponsor / Judge Follow-Up
subject: Follow-up from {{event_name}} on our project - {{your_name}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Thank you for judging our project during {{event_name}} last weekend. You suggested optimizing our indexing layer for {{admired_project}}, and I spent the last few days implementing that recommendation.

I refactored the pipeline in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}}. The updated benchmarks and codebase are available at {{portfolio}}.

Could I ask for your brief take on whether this revised implementation resolves the scaling bottleneck you identified?

Sincerely,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Reconnect with a hackathon judge or sponsor engineer with updates on project feedback received during evaluation.
toneNote: Action-oriented, demonstrating rapid iteration upon receiving feedback.
altOpeners: Thank you for evaluating our team's submission during {{event_name}} last weekend.
I was grateful for your technical critique of our implementation during the judging round at {{event_name}}.
Following up on your advice at {{event_name}} regarding our project's architecture.
whenToUse: Within 7 days of meeting a judge or sponsor engineer at a major hackathon or competition.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you did not implement the judge's feedback.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early in the week following the hackathon.
followUpNote: If they give positive feedback, ask about engineering internship or fresher openings.

name: Community Chat to DM (Discord/Slack/GitHub)
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, enjoyed our exchange in the public discussion on {{source_trigger}}! Your breakdown on handling state consistency really resonated.

As someone building in {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}.

Quick follow-up question: in your daily work at {{company}}, do you run into similar constraints when deploying to distributed clusters?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Transition a productive public community thread (Discord, Slack, GitHub Discussions) into a professional DM.
toneNote: Informal, respectful of community norms, references public thread context.
altOpeners: Reaching out following our discussion in the community thread on {{source_trigger}}.
Saw your response in the public forum regarding {{source_trigger}}.
Enjoyed exchanging thoughts in the community chat on {{source_trigger}}.
whenToUse: When you have previously exchanged public messages on Discord, Slack, Reddit, or GitHub Discussions.
whenNotToUse: Do not send unsolicited DMs to members without a prior public interaction.
sendWindowNote: Send within a few hours of the public exchange while context is top of mind.
followUpNote: If no reply, do not pester; respect private boundaries.

name: Booth / Career-Fair Recruiter Follow-Up
subject: Follow-up from {{event_name}} booth - {{your_name}} ({{role}})
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

It was great speaking with you at {{company}}'s booth during {{event_name}}. We briefly discussed how my background in {{primary_skill}} aligns with your upcoming {{role}} requisitions.

As mentioned, I recently {{proof_point}}. My full code samples and resume are available at {{portfolio}}.

Could you share if application links for the {{role}} opening have opened for our batch?

Thank you for your time,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Follow up with a recruiter after speaking in person at a campus booth or tech career fair.
toneNote: Polite, brisk, provides verified resume link and highlights conversation topic.
altOpeners: It was a pleasure speaking with you at {{company}}'s booth during {{event_name}} yesterday.
Thank you for taking a few minutes to discuss {{company}}'s engineering team at {{event_name}}.
Following up on our conversation at the {{event_name}} career fair regarding {{role}} opportunities.
whenToUse: Within 24 to 48 hours of speaking with a company representative at a career fair or booth.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if you did not actually meet at the event.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is the morning immediately following the career fair.
followUpNote: Follow up after 7 business days with gentle-follow-up.

name: Specific Job-ID Referral Ask with Forwardable Fit Summary
subject: Referral inquiry: {{role}} (Job ID: {{job_id}}) - {{your_name}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I hope your week is going well. I am preparing to apply for {{company}}'s {{role}} opening (Job ID: {{job_id}}).

To make this as quick as possible for you, here is a 3-line summary formatted for your internal referral form:
- Candidate: {{your_name}} ({{your_email}})
- Core Tech: {{primary_skill}} (evidence: {{proof_point}})
- Code & Portfolio: {{portfolio}}

If you feel comfortable submitting this, I would be immensely grateful. If current bandwidth does not permit, I completely understand and appreciate your time.

Warmly,
{{your_name}}
description: Provide a warm contact with an exact 3-line forwardable blurb that takes them under 30 seconds to paste into the referral portal.
toneNote: Frictionless, structured, ultra-considerate of referrer's busy workday.
altOpeners: I am preparing an application for {{company}}'s {{role}} opening (Job ID: {{job_id}}) and put together a forwardable blurb.
Following up on our discussions, I found the active requisition for {{role}} at {{company}} under Job ID {{job_id}}.
I wanted to reach out regarding the open {{role}} position at {{company}} with a pre-written fit summary.
whenToUse: Strictly for alumni, mutual connections, or engineers who already know you or your work.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked for strangers. Never request a referral from someone who has never heard of you.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday early evening.
followUpNote: If submitted, thank them immediately with thank-you-referral-submitted.

name: Thank You After Referral Submitted
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Thank you so much for taking the time out of your busy schedule to submit my referral for the {{role}} opening at {{company}}!

I received the automated confirmation from the recruitment portal. I will keep you posted as the process moves forward, and I really appreciate you putting your word behind my profile.

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
description: Express genuine gratitude immediately after a contact submits an internal employee referral.
toneNote: Grateful, gracious, brief, zero additional requests.
altOpeners: Thank you so much for taking the time to submit my referral for {{role}} at {{company}}!
I just received the confirmation notification from {{company}}'s careers portal, thank you!
Grateful for your support submitting the internal referral for {{company}}.
whenToUse: Send within 24 hours of receiving confirmation that your referral was logged in the portal.
whenNotToUse: Never ask for another favor or referral in this note.
sendWindowNote: Send promptly after the submission confirmation is received.
followUpNote: Update them only when a significant milestone occurs (e.g. interview scheduled or completed).

name: Referral Status Nudge (~14 Days)
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Hope you are having a productive week! Checking in briefly about {{days_since_last_contact}} days after you kindly submitted my referral for the {{role}} opening.

I have not heard back from the recruitment team yet, which is completely normal given volume. If there is any additional project breakdown or code repository I can provide on my end ({{portfolio}}), please let me know.

Thanks again for supporting my application,
{{your_name}}
description: Gently check in with your internal referrer after two weeks of silence from the talent acquisition team.
toneNote: Low pressure, helpful, appreciative, zero entitlement.
altOpeners: Checking in briefly about two weeks following your referral submission for {{role}} at {{company}}.
Wanted to send a quiet check-in regarding the {{role}} application referred {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago.
Reaching out with a quick status check on the {{company}} referral portal.
whenToUse: Send roughly 12 to 14 days after the referral was submitted if talent acquisition has not initiated contact.
whenNotToUse: Do not send if the recruiter has already initiated technical screening or contacted you.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday afternoon.
followUpNote: If no recruiter movement occurs after 3 weeks, transition focus to other pipeline companies.

name: Give-First Note Before Any Ask
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your team's recent discussion around {{admired_project}} at {{company}}. While building with {{primary_skill}}, I came across an open-source testing harness that addresses this exact edge case: {{portfolio}}.

Thought this might save your team a few hours of sprint debugging. No reply needed, just wanted to share something genuinely helpful!

Best,
{{your_name}}
description: Share an authentic technical resource, benchmark, or tool without requesting any job or referral.
toneNote: Generous, community-minded, zero transactional expectation.
altOpeners: Saw your team discussing {{admired_project}} benchmarks and wanted to share a useful tool.
Came across an open-source library that directly mirrors what you were building for {{admired_project}}.
I noticed your public discussion around {{primary_skill}} tooling and thought this might be useful.
whenToUse: When connecting with high-caliber engineers before establishing any transactional relationship.
whenNotToUse: Never attach a resume or ask for a referral in this message.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday mornings or weekends.
followUpNote: Allow the relationship to develop naturally. Never pivot to a job ask within the same week.

name: Post-Online-Assessment Note to Recruiter
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I wanted to confirm that I completed and submitted the online technical assessment for {{company}}'s {{role}} opening earlier today.

Thank you for setting up the evaluation link. I enjoyed working through the test problems and look forward to hearing your team's timeline for scheduling the technical rounds.

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
description: Confirm completion of an online coding assessment neutrally without speculating about scores.
toneNote: Composed, process-oriented, neutral, does not comment on test difficulty.
altOpeners: Confirming completion of the technical assessment for the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
I wanted to confirm that I have submitted the online assessment for the {{role}} position.
Reaching out to verify that my test submission for {{company}} {{role}} was logged.
whenToUse: Send within a few hours of submitting an official online coding assessment (HackerRank, Codility, etc.).
whenNotToUse: Do not speculate on your score, justify failed test cases, or ask for answers.
sendWindowNote: Send promptly after test submission is confirmed.
followUpNote: Allow 5 to 7 business days for automated batch grading before checking in.

name: Thank You After Technical Round
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Thank you for your time during our technical interview today. I particularly enjoyed our discussion around {{interviewer_topic}}.

Thinking further about that trade-off, I appreciated your insight on balancing memory overhead against lookup speed in production. It reinforced my excitement about the engineering bar at {{company}}.

Thanks again for an engaging session,
{{your_name}}
description: Thank a technical interviewer by reflecting on a specific problem or architectural trade-off discussed in the session.
toneNote: Thoughtful, intellectually engaged, references exact technical conversation.
altOpeners: Thank you for taking the time to conduct our technical interview for {{company}} today.
I really enjoyed our discussion during the technical screen for {{role}} at {{company}}.
Grateful for the engaging technical round we had today covering {{company}} engineering.
whenToUse: Send within 24 hours of completing a technical interview with an engineer or hiring manager.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked if interviewer_topic is empty. Generic thank-you notes add zero value.
sendWindowNote: Send late afternoon on the same day or early morning following the interview.
followUpNote: Wait for the recruiter to communicate official interview outcomes.

name: Silence After Final Round (Day 7+)
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Following up on my final interview round with the {{role}} team at {{company}}, completed {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago.

I really enjoyed meeting the team and discussing their technical priorities. I know hiring committee reviews require coordination across multiple calendars, so I wanted to check in quietly to see if there are any updates regarding next steps.

Thank you for your guidance through this process,
{{your_name}}
description: Follow up calmly on final-round interview outcomes after at least 7 days of silence from the talent team.
toneNote: Patient, calm, respectful of extended hiring committee deliberations.
altOpeners: Following up on our final interview round held {{days_since_last_contact}} days ago for {{role}} at {{company}}.
Checking in regarding next steps following my final round with the {{company}} engineering team.
Reaching out for a quiet status update following my final interviews for {{role}}.
whenToUse: Only offered when days_since_last_contact >= 7 days following the final interview round.
whenNotToUse: Never send before 7 full business days have elapsed.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday morning around 10:00 AM.
followUpNote: If no reply after an additional 7 days, send final-polite-loop-closure.

name: Real Competing Deadline Note
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I wanted to share a transparent update on my recruitment timeline. I have received an offer from another organization that requires a decision by {{availability_date}}.

{{company}} remains my top choice due to the engineering team's work on {{admired_project}}. Because of this deadline, I wanted to ask if your team might be able to expedite the decision timeline for my {{role}} interviews before {{availability_date}}.

I appreciate your support and completely understand if current scheduling does not permit an earlier turnaround.

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
description: Politely inform a recruiter of a genuine, verified decision deadline with another employer to accelerate your timeline.
toneNote: Calm, transparent, ethical, expresses genuine preference for target company without ultimatums.
altOpeners: I am reaching out with an update regarding my timeline, as I have received an offer with a decision deadline.
Wanted to share an update on my current interview cycle, as I am managing a concrete offer deadline.
Writing with transparency regarding an active decision deadline on my end.
whenToUse: Strictly when you possess a real, written offer with an active expiration deadline.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked without user confirmation checkbox. Never fabricate fake deadlines or competing offers.
sendWindowNote: Send immediately upon receiving the competing offer's written deadline.
followUpNote: Prepare to make a final decision by availability_date regardless of response.

name: Polite Withdrawal From Process
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I am writing to share that I have accepted an offer with another company, and would like to respectfully withdraw my application for the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.

I was genuinely impressed by the engineers I spoke with and appreciated the thoughtful conversations throughout the interview stages. I hope we can stay in touch on LinkedIn as our paths cross in the industry.

Thank you for your time and guidance,
{{your_name}}
description: Formally withdraw from an active interview process with prompt courtesy, leaving doors open for the future.
toneNote: Courteous, appreciative of time invested, definitive yet warm.
altOpeners: I am writing to formally withdraw my application for the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
Wanted to notify you promptly that I am withdrawing from consideration for the {{role}} position.
Reaching out to share that I have accepted another opportunity and am closing my candidacy.
whenToUse: Send as soon as you have signed an offer with another employer while actively interviewing with this team.
whenNotToUse: Do not send if you have not finalized written offer terms elsewhere.
sendWindowNote: Send promptly within 24 hours of accepting an offer.
followUpNote: No follow-up needed. Connect with the recruiter on LinkedIn.

name: 15-Minute Advice Ask to Senior Engineer
subject: Quick technical advice on {{primary_skill}} architecture - {{your_name}}
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I have been following your technical insights at {{company}} regarding {{primary_skill}}. I am currently facing a concrete architectural decision on a project where I recently {{proof_point}}.

I am weighing whether to decouple my queue consumers early or keep them inside a modular monolith until throughput demands distributed workers. Given your experience with high-scale services at {{company}}, I would value your quick perspective.

Would you have 10 minutes for a brief call, or could I email two short questions?

Sincerely,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Ask for a brief perspective on one specific career or technical architecture decision the sender is actively facing.
toneNote: Humble, focused on a specific decision, avoids generic "how do I get hired" prompts.
altOpeners: I have been following your technical engineering insights at {{company}} regarding {{primary_skill}}.
Your career journey as a staff engineer at {{company}} represents the technical depth I hope to develop.
As an engineer navigating early architecture decisions in {{primary_skill}}, I value your perspective.
whenToUse: When seeking authentic technical mentoring from a senior or staff engineer on a specific fork in the road.
whenNotToUse: Do not use as a veiled job application or to ask for an immediate referral.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday through Thursday early evening.
followUpNote: If they offer guidance, write a thorough thank-you note sharing what you implemented.

name: Prospective Teammate Stack/Culture Question
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your work as an engineer at {{company}} on {{admired_project}}. As someone building with {{primary_skill}}, I recently {{proof_point}}.

Quick engineering question: how does your team structure integration testing between microservices before production rollout?

Curious to learn how your team approaches this challenge day-to-day.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
description: Ask a single specific question about day-to-day tooling and testing practices to a potential future teammate.
toneNote: Collegial, curious, respectful of time, strictly one question.
altOpeners: What testing framework and CI pipeline does your engineering group rely on at {{company}}?
How does your team at {{company}} manage code reviews and automated deployment checks?
Quick culture question: how much autonomous ownership do junior engineers have over feature specs at {{company}}?
whenToUse: When connecting with potential future engineering peers before or during application season.
whenNotToUse: Never ask multiple compound questions; stick strictly to one single inquiry.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is weekday afternoon.
followUpNote: Thank them for their response and do not pressure them into referrals.

name: Interview Process Questions to Recent Hire
template: Hi {{recipient_name}}, congratulations on joining {{company}} as a {{role}}! As a {{college}} student preparing for {{primary_skill}} interviews, I would love to connect and follow your journey as an early-career engineer on the team.
description: Connect with a recently joined fresher or junior engineer who navigated the recruitment bar in the past 6-12 months.
toneNote: Peer-level, congratulatory, zero referral ask, focused on interview preparation tips.
altOpeners: Hi {{recipient_name}}, great to see another early-career engineer joining {{company}}.
Hi {{recipient_name}}, congrats on your recent role at {{company}} on the tech team!
Hi {{recipient_name}}, saw your recent update joining {{company}} as a software engineer.
whenToUse: For connecting with engineers who joined the target company within the past year.
whenNotToUse: Do not ask for a referral in this touchpoint; recent hires often cannot refer candidates immediately.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is early evening.
followUpNote: After connecting, ask what topics appeared most frequently in their coding assessment.

name: One-Question Note After a Talk or Post
description: Send a laser-focused, ultra-concise technical follow-up question after reading a post or watching a conference talk.
toneNote: Ultra-crisp, 40 to 60 words, zero pleasantry overhead.
altOpeners: Loved your session on {{talk_topic}} at {{event_name}}.
Watched your presentation covering {{talk_topic}} at {{event_name}} yesterday.
Read your summary on {{talk_topic}} and had one quick follow-up question.
whenToUse: When you have a sharp, single technical question immediately after a tech talk, podcast, or post.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for lengthy multi-topic emails or generalized career queries.
sendWindowNote: Send within 24 hours of the talk while the topic is active.
followUpNote: If they answer, send a one-sentence thank-you and let the conversation conclude.

name: Re-Apply After Rejection
subject: Re-application for {{role}} at {{company}} - {{your_name}} update
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

I interviewed for the {{role}} opening with {{company}} earlier this year. While the timing was not right then, I took the team's feedback to heart and spent the last few months leveling up my technical foundations.

Since our last conversation: {{what_changed}}. In addition, I {{proof_point}} (documented code and tests: {{portfolio}}).

With {{company}} continuing to grow the {{role}} team, could we schedule a brief 10-minute check-in to see if my updated background qualifies for re-evaluation?

Best regards,
{{your_name}}
{{your_email}}
description: Re-engage a recruiter 6 months after an interview rejection by presenting verifiable technical growth and projects shipped since.
toneNote: Mature, growth-oriented, zero defensiveness, highlights newly acquired technical capabilities.
altOpeners: Following my interview cycle for {{role}} at {{company}} earlier this year, I spent the last two quarters strengthening my systems foundations.
I wanted to circle back following our interview cycle 6 months ago with a major update on my engineering work.
Reflecting on my previous technical interview with {{company}}, I focused on building depth in {{primary_skill}}.
whenToUse: Send at least 6 months after an interview loop when you have concrete, verifiable progress to demonstrate.
whenNotToUse: Hard blocked if what_changed is empty. Never re-apply without concrete new projects or skills.
sendWindowNote: Common practice is Tuesday or Wednesday morning.
followUpNote: If no reply after 10 business days, move forward and focus on other targets.

name: Reply to "No Openings Right Now"
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Thank you for the transparent update regarding hiring bandwidth for the {{role}} team at {{company}}.

I completely understand that headcount priorities shift. What technical signals or upcoming hiring quarters would you recommend I watch for as your engineering roadmap expands?

I will continue following {{company}}'s public updates and would love to stay connected on LinkedIn in the meantime.

Thanks again for your time,
{{your_name}}
description: Respond gracefully to a "no headcount" response by inquiring what technical signals or timing to watch for next.
toneNote: Gracious, professional, non-pushy, seeks future alignment signals.
altOpeners: Thank you for the quick and transparent update regarding current headcount at {{company}}.
I appreciate the prompt response regarding {{company}}'s hiring timelines.
Thanks for letting me know about the current hiring pause for {{role}} at {{company}}.
whenToUse: When a recruiter or founder politely declines due to lack of open positions or freeze.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the decline was due to severe technical screening failure.
sendWindowNote: Reply within 24 hours of receiving their note.
followUpNote: Check in after 3-4 months when a new quarter begins.

name: Reply to "Please Share Your Details"
description: Respond promptly and completely when a recruiter requests your candidate logistics (batch, notice, location, expected CTC).
toneNote: Precise, operational, formatted for immediate HR database entry.
altOpeners: Thank you for reaching out! Here are the requested candidate details for {{role}} at {{company}}.
Delighted to share my information regarding the {{role}} opening at {{company}}.
Here are my logistics and technical details as requested for {{company}}'s {{role}} team.
whenToUse: When a recruiter has replied requesting availability, notice period, location preferences, or graduation batch.
whenNotToUse: Do not send unsolicited as a first message.
sendWindowNote: Send promptly within 2-4 hours of receiving the recruiter's inquiry.
followUpNote: If no reply within 4 business days, follow up with gentle-follow-up.

name: Reply to "Open to Other Roles?" / Role Mismatch
template:
Hi {{recipient_name}},

Thank you for considering my background! While I appreciate the thought regarding alternative roles, my deep hands-on expertise and project work are centered around {{role_family}} development.

I specialize in {{primary_skill}}, and recently {{proof_point}} (verified projects: {{portfolio}}). I want to ensure I bring maximum immediate impact to {{company}} where my core strengths lie.

Does {{company}} currently have openings in the {{role_family}} group where my technical background would be a tighter match?

Warmly,
{{your_name}}
description: Redirect a recruiter proposing an mismatched role towards your true core engineering family while preserving goodwill.
toneNote: Honest about engineering strengths, collaborative, redirects to the right role family.
altOpeners: Thank you for considering my profile for {{company}}'s team.
Appreciate you reviewing my background and exploring potential fits across {{company}}.
Thank you for the thoughtful suggestion regarding alternative openings at {{company}}.
whenToUse: When an HR recruiter offers an unrelated role (e.g. QA, technical support, sales engineering) but you want software engineering.
whenNotToUse: Do not use if the proposed role is actually an acceptable career step for your goals.
sendWindowNote: Reply within 24 hours of receiving the offer to interview for an alternate role.
followUpNote: If they confirm an opening in your target role family, send reply-share-your-details.
